title: Folio 6: The Sultan and the Lion | The Honest Historian – Stories from Beyhaqi
description:
Sick with fever, his club missed and his spear snapped, a young prince faced a wounded lion with nothing but his hands. Beyhaqi saw Masud of Ghazni hunt lions alone, stand barefoot in the snow, and kill eight lions in a day. But what does a lion hunt tell us about a king who would soon face enemies no spear could stop?

Source: Tarikh-e Beyhaqi, volume six: the portrait of Amir Masud's habits and hunting (section on lion hunting: his training, winter hunts, the lion near Kikanan on the road to Multan, the elephant hunt in India, eight lions in one day near Herat, Bu Sahl Zawzani's Arabic verses), read in the Persian text (Ganjoor, Fayyaz edition p. 143); background from Encyclopaedia Iranica and Wikipedia ('Mas'ud I of Ghazni', 'Bahram V').
Retold in English from the Persian original by Mehdi Rahmani and narrated with an AI rendering of his own voice.
